compiled_state.description:
## Summary

A completion-verification run started through `verify_completion_start` never exposes its
`findings` to the caller. `gate_status(job_id)` returns `findings: null` even after the run
finishes with `verdict: "FAIL"`, and `verify_completion_status(ticket)` reports only
`{"ok": false, "verdict": "unsigned", "reason": "ticket has no signature"}` — the absence of
a signature, which is a consequence of the FAIL rather than a reason for it.

The findings exist. The synchronous `verify_completion` tool returns them in full, with
per-criterion `met` booleans, `detail` text, file citations, and `remediation`. The async
surface simply does not surface them, and `AGENTS.md` directs agents to prefer the async
surface precisely because the sync one can blow the client's ~60s deadline.

So the only way to learn why an async FAIL failed is to run the whole verification again
through the sync tool — a second, billable, full LLM pass for information the first pass
already computed.

## Evidence

Observed 2026-09-19 on `f3b2-6bb8-a643-4025` and `1d89-2206-bb64-4d98`.

Async runs (`verify_completion_start`, jobs `1789885325274338093-…`, `1789885325281626578-…`,
then re-runs `1789886837558203964-…`, `1789886837564434373-…`):
- `gate_status` → `status: "passed"`, `verdict: "FAIL"`, `findings: null`.
- `verify_completion_status` → `verdict: "unsigned"`, `reason: "ticket has no signature"`.
- No `COMPLETION_VERDICT` sidecar was written for either ticket, so the store held no
  record to fall back on either.

Sync run on the same ticket and the same `ref`, immediately afterwards, returned 2 findings
with severity `high`, exact line citations, and a `remediation` block. For `f3b2` it named
the unmet criterion (`docs/releasing.md` missing the `mcp` major-ignore statement and
retaining stale `pip/pydantic` wording); for `1d89` it named the missing
`pyproject.toml:353-356` uv-pin reference. Both were real, actionable, and correct.

Cost of the workaround, measured from the sync runs' own `metrics`: `f3b2` 72.7s total /
65.4s LLM, `1d89` 88.1s total / 80.6s LLM — each a full duplicate pass.

Note the sidecar IS written for FAIL in general: `01c4-cca2-ec11-4530` and
`021d-ae08-ecd6-4495` both carry `verdict: "FAIL"` sidecars. Whatever suppressed it for
these two runs is a second, related gap — an async FAIL left no durable trace anywhere.

## Why this matters

The guidance steers agents to the async surface, and the async surface is the one that
discards the result's substance. An agent that follows the documented path gets an
unexplained FAIL, and the cheapest route to the explanation is paying for the run twice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `gate_status` returns the findings for a completed completion-verification job.
- [ ] `verify_completion_status` distinguishes "verified and failed" from "never verified".
- [ ] A FAIL reported through the async surface is accompanied by its per-criterion results.
- [ ] A completion-verification FAIL started asynchronously writes a `COMPLETION_VERDICT`
      sidecar, matching the sync surface's behaviour.
- [ ] Reading an async run's findings requires no second LLM pass.
- [ ] A regression test covers async-started completion verification that ends in FAIL.
- [ ] A regression test asserts the async and sync surfaces report the same verdict and the
      same findings for the same ticket and ref.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` or `docs/mcp-reference.md` states where async gate findings
      are read from.
compiled_state.title: Async completion-verification FAIL discards its findings, forcing a duplicate billable run to learn why
